$description: The grammar as data. Every rule in GRAMMAR.md, with the authority it carries. Only an invariant can fail a build, and an invariant is a mechanical truth about the artifact, never a design judgement. Policy is evaluated and reported. A preference carries its number. Knowledge is what was learned, with its source. Precedent is never declared here: it is computed from the record.
$layers: The layers, as data, because the site used to hand-write this table and it drifted exactly as knowledge.drift-by-transcription predicts: it went on saying a validator enforced Layer 0 and that undeclared drift failed CI, long after both stopped being true. A layer's character is a claim about governance, so it belongs where the rules are and is projected into anything that displays it.

layers.name: Meaning
layers.what: Semantic roles, derived by the engine from six seeds. The one vocabulary everything else speaks — consistency is predictability of meaning, not visual sameness.
layers.governance: one author · never forked · every role decided

layers.name: Behavior
layers.what: Headless focus, keyboard and ARIA primitives. A solved primitive is imported, never reimplemented — a second focus trap is a second set of bugs, and it is the copy that rots.

layers.name: Recipes
layers.what: Styled compositions of meaning and behaviour. Copy the source, keep the two imports, restyle freely.
layers.governance: forkable by default · eject is a feature

layers.name: Local
layers.what: Feature-owned one-offs. No permission required; a raw value here is reported like anywhere else, and declaring it makes it evidence.
layers.governance: free · candidacy computed by reuse, promotion decided by a hand

layers.name: Machine
layers.what: The part that makes the freedom safe: every projection regenerates from the record, and a build fails only when the artifact cannot be produced from it. Drift never fails CI — undeclared drift is reported, declared drift is evidence.

rules.statement: Every line of .strata/decisions.jsonl is a decision: an id, a kind, a hand, a time, a surface.
rules.reason: The record is the source; a projection of a record that cannot be read is a guess.
rules.source: substrate/src/decision.ts

rules.statement: ledger.json, semantic.css, tokens.json and overrides.json are byte for byte what the record projects.
rules.reason: An artifact that cannot be faithfully produced from the record is not a projection of it, and a hand edit there is a decision nobody made.
rules.incident: The stylesheet that said surface chroma 0.012 while the engine computed 0.006. Nobody chose that; transcription did.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › The engine is the only author

rules.statement: Every token the engine emits has a fallback, nothing else does, and every chain ends in a literal.
rules.reason: A cut token collapses instead of disappearing; a token with no floor, or a floor that loops, would fail every consumer silently at computed-value time.
rules.source: src/theme/ledger.ts

rules.statement: Every var(--name) a stylesheet reaches for names a custom property something defines.
rules.reason: An undefined custom property is an invalid declaration paid at the consumer, invisible in the diff — the behaviour this repo calls the worst available.
rules.source: src/theme/ledger.ts

rules.statement: Components and the site speak semantic names — --accent, --surface-raised — never a hex, an oklch(), an rgb() or a green-500. A literal that must exist declares itself: a comment containing deviation: and the reason.
rules.reason: Consistency is not visual sameness; it is predictability of meaning. Two screens that share nothing but this vocabulary still cohere. Declared drift is promotion-candidate telemetry, not a violation.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › Semantic names only

rules.statement: semantic.css and tokens.json are projections of generateTheme.ts through the ledger. Regenerate; never edit.
rules.reason: The repo grew its own drift in week one by transcription. The invariant projections.match-record is the mechanical half of this rule; this is the practice.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › The engine is the only author

rules.statement: A theme is six seeds, and light is not inverted dark: light appearances compile accents at 0.87× chroma and lower lightness.
rules.reason: A light accent that merely inverts fails AA on paper. The engine encodes the correction so no one has to remember it.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › A theme is six seeds

rules.statement: Warmth tints every neutral toward paper or slate; a pure mid-grey is never emitted.
rules.reason: A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered. Even grey is a chosen colour.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › Warmth tints every neutral

rules.statement: Energy sets easing, duration and radius together.
rules.reason: Motion personality that stops at duration produces themes that feel mislabeled.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › Energy buys shape as well as speed

rules.statement: One family. Hierarchy is weight, size and measure — never a second voice.
rules.reason: v0.2 shipped a variable serif with italic accents and a green display line; the owner's correction is the record: overly designed text that did not meet the design grammar.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › One family

rules.statement: Mono is for what is read as data — labels, values, receipts — and never for prose.
rules.reason: When a compiled prompt was dressed as a developer tool the owner wrote that it should not look like code. A value in mono is honest; a paragraph in mono is a costume.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › Mono is for what is read as data

rules.statement: Labels are microtype: small, tracked caps, faint ink. The accent never carries a label.
rules.reason: A kicker in the accent colour is a second voice competing with the heading it introduces.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › Labels are microtype

rules.statement: Monochrome by default; colour is a choice, and a monochrome accent is ink.
rules.reason: A tool is unobtrusive so the user's own work carries the colour. A mid grey at the chromatic lightness fails AA on paper and reads as disabled everywhere.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › Monochrome by default

rules.statement: Lines, not shadows. Every level is a 1px rule and an alpha wash.
rules.reason: Neither reference paints a drop shadow anywhere; --shadow-color is cut in the ledger, so the elevation tokens keep their offsets and paint nothing.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › Lines, not shadows

rules.statement: Nothing bounces, and there are two radii: a control and a panel.
rules.reason: A sheet that overshoots and the one soft shape on an architectural page were both personality the chrome should not have.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › Nothing bounces

rules.statement: The appearance control is a dot after the wordmark: faint ink when monochrome, the accent when there is one. A real button with a name, reachable by tab.
rules.reason: Appearance costs nothing and answers to nobody; a labelled switch in the navigation read as one more thing to decide before you could work. Quiet and hidden are different things.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › The appearance control is the mark

rules.statement: Dark is the first ground; light is one flipped bit.
rules.reason: Gallery is Obsidian with appearance flipped and nothing else changed, because the two poles are one theme's two grounds.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The voice › Dark is the first ground

rules.statement: A focus trap, roving tabindex, arrow-key order, Escape and backdrop dismissal are solved primitives. They are imported, never reimplemented — not because an arrangement of them could be incorrect, but because a second implementation is a second set of bugs.
rules.reason: It is the copy that rots: the original gets the fix and the fork keeps the defect, silently, for as long as nobody diffs them. It is also what lets a region move at all — behaviour travels with a component that consumed it, and stays behind when a component wrote its own.
rules.incident: This is the part everyone quietly rebuilds badly when they eject from a monolithic system, so it is the part an eject must preserve.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 1 — Behavior

rules.statement: A backdrop click is a click on the <dialog> element itself: e.target === dialog is the whole implementation.
rules.reason: Anything cleverer breaks the moment the sheet scrolls.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 1 — Behavior › A backdrop click

rules.statement: Reduced motion is honoured in the generated CSS and re-checked by applyTheme at runtime.
rules.reason: Inline style properties beat media queries; a runtime engine that ignores the preference silently undoes the stylesheet's promise.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 1 — Behavior › Reduced motion

rules.statement: Recipes speak tokens and consume behaviour; everything else is theirs. Copy a recipe, keep the two imports, restyle freely.
rules.reason: The adversarial relationship with a design system ends the moment taking the code is sanctioned.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 2 — Recipes

rules.statement: One filled action per surface. Primary is filled; Secondary is an edge; Ghost is bare text.
rules.reason: When three calls to action carry the same chrome, the screen has no point.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 2 — Recipes › One filled action per surface

rules.statement: Disabled is opacity 0.45 on the whole control, not a third palette.
rules.reason: A disabled variant per colour multiplies the matrix without adding meaning; a uniform veil reads as off everywhere at once.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 2 — Recipes › Disabled

rules.statement: Status colours are ink and wash, split by role: --danger is ink, --danger-soft is a fill. One name per role.
rules.reason: A border alpha and a fill alpha doing different jobs under one name is how 34 accidental alphas happen.
rules.incident: The stylesheet with thirty-four accidental white alphas.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 2 — Recipes › Status colors

rules.statement: Build one-offs in your feature. No one reviews expression there; Layer 0's vocabulary still applies.
rules.reason: Promotion is earned by usage, never granted by proposal.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 3 — Local

rules.statement: A shape that appears this many times, independently, is a promotion candidate.
rules.reason: One is taste; nine of the same shape is a missing token. Three is where the report starts saying so.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Credo › Less but better

rules.statement: Nothing runs, warns or flags while someone is designing. Evaluation happens at ready, at check, and when asked.
rules.reason: A design in progress fails any check by definition, so a tool that reports mid-drag is measuring the wrong moment and reads as policing by volume.
rules.incident: The slot layer priced every drag against a contract and wrote the cost into source. It was removed — but its premise, that an arrangement can be scored against a declaration, outlived the code and fused with the reporter: `layer1.correctness-not-taste` went on asserting it for months after the thing that justified it was gone. It is not residue, it is an attractor. An agent with no exposure to the slot layer re-derived it from scratch in this repository, arguing that a layer 1 finding should be a violation rather than an observation — reasoning locally from "the code is wrong" to "the check should say so." Deleting the code does not inoculate against the idea. Expect it back, and read for it.
rules.source: README.md › Governance

rules.statement: Hand-written projections drift from the engine within a week.
rules.reason: Week one of this repo: the CSS said 0.012 where the engine computed 0.006.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › Layer 0 — Meaning › The engine is the only author

rules.statement: Cutting the accent collapses the whole colour tier to ink, and focus stays visible through it.
rules.reason: The fallback table is written as a gate: --accent → --ink, everything accent-derived follows, --focus-ring lands on ink last.
rules.source: src/theme/ledger.ts

rules.statement: A move is never wrong at the page level; what it costs is code, and code is malleable to the design.
rules.reason: The reviewer makes the code fit and never moves anything back — undoing a designer's move is how a designer stops believing the tool.
rules.source: README.md › Structure is moved, not declared

rules.statement: Every decision names two hands: `decided`, who could have chosen otherwise, and `written`, whose hand ran the command. Either may be an agent. The test is one question — who could have chosen otherwise? Four cases settle it. A specified outcome, where the target and the value were both named to you: decided by the person who named them. A specified intent with the outcome left open: decided by you, with their instruction in the reason. Unprompted work — wiring, cleanup, a consequence you noticed: decided by you. Something you proposed and they confirmed: decided by them.
rules.reason: The record carried one `by`, and what it recorded was the channel that ran the command, so thirty-four decisions a person made came back reading as an agent's. A record of judgements and a log of keystrokes are different objects; only the first is worth reading later.
rules.incident: Week one of the record: every imported line said `agent`, and not one of those decisions was.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The machine layer › Who chose, and whose hand wrote it

rules.statement: Using a token is not deciding one. Nothing writes a decision for a `var(--x)` already in a recipe; the record holds departures and rulings — a cut, an override, a move, a pick, a declared deviation — and consumers are evidence, computed by `explain` and `check` when asked.
rules.reason: A record that logged every use would be a usage log, and a usage log is read by nobody. Reading the record as departures and rulings is what makes thirty lines worth more than thirty thousand.
rules.source: GRAMMAR.md › The machine layer › Use is not a decision
